rfm_tuples.claim_text: FY2025 (ended Jan 31, 2026) 10-K: Net sales decreased 4.0% to $14.8B with comparable sales down 3.1%. Operating income was $624M (4.0% margin) vs $433M prior year — but this included a $129M one-time gain on legal settlement (credit card interchange fee lawsuit). On an adjusted non-GAAP basis, adjusted operating income was $510M vs $509M prior year (essentially flat). Net income was $272M / $2.38 diluted EPS GAAP; adjusted $186M / $1.62 EPS. Cash from ops $1.4B vs $648M prior year (driven by $203M inventory liquidation + $130M AP build, not earnings).
rfm_tuples.R: Net sales decreased 4.0%, to $14.8 billion, with comparable sales down 3.1%... Operating income was $624 million compared to $433 million in the prior year... adjusted operating income was $510 million compared to $509 million in the prior year
rfm_tuples.f_method: internal_consistency — strip the $129M one-time legal gain and the working capital release from the headline turnaround narrative
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K MD&A + Consolidated Statements of Operations + Cash Flow Statement
rfm_tuples.M_value: Excluding $129M legal-settlement gain, FY2025 GAAP operating income = $495M (3.2% margin), BELOW the $433M prior-year GAAP figure. Adjusted operating income flat YoY ($510M vs $509M). Operating cash flow doubled YoY only because inventory was drawn down $203M and AP built $130M — neither repeatable. Top-line decline is third consecutive year of contraction: $17.5B (2023) -> $16.2B (2024) -> $15.5B (2025) total revenue. Comparable sales -3.1% on top of -4.2% prior year is cumulative -7% same-store decline over two years.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: Disclosed. Management framing of 'operating income $624M vs $433M' is technically true but obscures that adjusted opex is flat and the GAAP improvement is one-time legal cash. Honesty-alpha: this is disclosed bad news, but the framing in MD&A is deceptively positive.

Issuer's framing as growth-recovery narrative is contradicted by their own EPS guide.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: Beneath the soft language of 'flat sales and margin recovery,' the EPS midpoint guidance implies -20% adjusted EPS decline. Combined with Q3 FY25 operating margin contraction, the FY2026 plan is for continued earnings deterioration, not stabilization. Market drawdown of -46% appears to be pricing this correctly.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Credit ratings: 'During 2024, S&P downgraded our senior unsecured credit rating from BB to BB- and Moody's downgraded our rating from Ba3 to B1. During 2025, Moody's further downgraded our senior unsecured credit rating from B1 to B3.' rfm_tuples.R: During 2025, Moody's further downgraded our senior unsecured credit rating from B1 to B3... we issued $360 million aggregate principal amount of 10.000% senior secured notes due 2030 and received proceeds of $357 million, net of the debt discount. The notes are guaranteed by certain of our subsidiaries. Certain of these guarantees are secured by eleven distribution centers and E-commerce Fulfillment Centers... as well as the equity interests in one of our subsidiaries.
rfm_tuples.R_unredacted_quote: the interest rate on the notes due May 2031 have increased 175 basis points since their issuance due to the coupon adjustment provision
rfm_tuples.f_method: credit_event_disclosure — verify the financial gravity of consecutive multi-notch downgrades and the secured-notes pledge
rfm_tuples.M_value: Moody's B3 is 5 notches below investment grade (Ba1 is one notch below IG; B3 is 5 below). Three downgrades over 2 fiscal years (Ba3->B1->B3 by Moody's; BB->BB- by S&P, with S&P explicitly noted as 'further downgrades by S&P would cause cost of borrowing to further increase'). The 10.000% coupon on 2030 secured notes vs 4.25% coupon on legacy 2025 notes that just matured = ~575 bps cost-of-capital widening. Distribution centers are now pledged as collateral — exhausting an unencumbered-assets pool that was previously a Kohl's-specific liquidity backstop. Coupon adjustment on 3.375% 2031 notes = +175 bps embedded auto-stepup. This is a Caa-bound trajectory.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: Disclosed. Mode B finding: the issuer notes 'further downgrades by Moody's do not trigger incremental interest rate increases' — i.e., management is normalizing the runway to deeper sub-investment-grade. Pledging distribution centers as collateral on a 10% secured note is a late-stage retail-distress balance-sheet move.

rfm_tuples.claim_text: Inventory and working capital: Merchandise inventories declined $203M YoY in FY2025 (from cash flow statement: '$203M' inventory reduction was the largest single contributor to the $732M YoY swing in operating cash flow). January 31, 2026 inventory $2.7B vs prior year ~$2.9B. However, Q3 FY2025 10-Q (Nov 1, 2025) showed inventory of $3,895M — up sharply from the $2,945M Feb 1 2025 audited balance — implying a $1B intra-year inventory build before the Q4 sell-down.
rfm_tuples.R: merchandise inventories balance was $2.7 billion... Merchandise inventories 3,895 [Nov 1, 2025] 2,945 [Feb 1, 2025] 4,099 [Nov 2, 2024]
rfm_tuples.f_method: balance_sheet_cross_period — reconcile Q3 10-Q inventory peak vs Q4 ending inventory and infer markdown intensity
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-Q (Q3 FY2025) Balance Sheet + 10-K FY2025 Balance Sheet + Statement of Cash Flows
rfm_tuples.M_value: Inventory peaked at $3.9B at Q3-end (Nov 1, 2025), then sold down to $2.7B by Jan 31, 2026 — a 31% reduction in 13 weeks. Q4 typically sees seasonal sell-down, but the prior year (Q3 ending Nov 2, 2024) inventory was $4.1B selling down to $2.9B by Feb 1, 2025 — i.e., a 29% Q4 sell-down. So Q4 sell-down intensity was comparable, but absolute exit inventory is at multi-year low ($2.7B), suggesting either tight Q4 demand control OR thin-shelves-going-into-Q1. Q4 gross margin held at 37.5% (+34 bps) suggesting markdowns were controlled — but the FY2026 plan implies further inventory tightness.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A: Confirmed. Disclosed inventory management. No discrepancy. Notable as a positive operational data point in an otherwise negative pattern — and partially explains the $1.4B operating cash flow.
